policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'an apostle of Christ Jesus', the order Christ-then-Jesus of the base lemma; the RP order would give 'Jesus Christ'.

ASV renders the clause in v6 ('or whether we are comforted, it is for your comfort'), so the omission is excluded; the two retained readings differ only in punctuation spacing, which no English wording can distinguish.

ASV places the 'whether we are comforted, it is for your comfort' clause in v6 and v7 carries nothing answering to it: 'and our hope for you is stedfast' proceeds directly from the verse opening, so the added clause is absent here.
ASV 'as ye are partakers' renders either particle; the base and RP forms are English-equivalent and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'concerning our affliction' renders either preposition; the pair is English-equivalent in this construction and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'which befell us in Asia' supplies an object English idiom requires of 'befall' whether or not the dative pronoun stands in the Greek, so the wording does not distinguish the addition.

ASV 'we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power' places both modifiers after the verb, reordering the base lemma's adverbial phrase as well; the English order is its own and does not report the Greek order.
ASV renders a future, 'and will deliver', where the RP present would give 'delivereth'; the mapped textual note offers only a different construal of the following clause, not the present tense.
ASV reads 'on our behalf', the first person pronoun of the base lemma; the RP second person would give 'on your behalf'.
ASV reads 'in holiness and sincerity of God', rendering the base lemma; the variant would give 'in simplicity' or 'singleness', which the ASV does not have here.
The unit turns on the article before 'God', which ASV's 'of God' cannot show either way.

ASV joins the phrases asyndetically, 'in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom', with no rendering of the conjunction the WH reading prefixes; ASV renders the other connectives of this verse.
ASV reads 'and I hope ye will acknowledge unto the end' with nothing answering to the added conjunction, though it renders the earlier one in this same verse as 'or even acknowledge'.
ASV reads 'in the day of our Lord Jesus'; the possessive renders the pronoun the omission would drop.
ASV 'to come first unto you' follows English order and renders the same words in either arrangement; the RP article on the adverb leaves no English trace.
ASV's text reads 'a second benefit', with 'Or, grace' in the margin, rendering the base lemma; the WH 'joy' is not the reading the ASV text carries.
ASV 'that ye might have' renders either verb; the two are English-equivalent here and the verse's only note concerns the noun, not this word.
ASV distinguishes the two verbs within this verse, rendering this one 'was thus minded' and reserving 'purpose' for the deliberative verb that follows; the RP reading would make both the same verb.
ASV reads 'our word toward you is not yea and nay', a present; the RP aorist would give 'was not'.
The unit turns on where the postpositive conjunction stands among the same words; ASV 'For the Son of God' renders both arrangements alike.
ASV reads 'Jesus Christ', the order of the base lemma; the WH order would give 'Christ Jesus'.
ASV reads 'wherefore also through him is the Amen', rendering the inferential particle the RP reading omits.
ASV reads 'through him is the Amen', the instrumental phrase of the base lemma; the RP reading would give 'in him', which the ASV uses earlier in this verse for the separate phrase.
